summary.text: A 72-year-old female was admitted on January 1, 2022 with septic shock secondary to a urinary tract infection. After inotropic treatment she developed necrosis of both hands and feet, underwent bilateral hand amputations on September 22, 2022 and bilateral transtibial amputations on October 26, 2022, giving quadruple amputation.

Transtibial prostheses were fitted and inpatient rehabilitation began on December 21, 2022. Upper-extremity wounds were unhealed at rehabilitation onset, preventing upper-limb prostheses and grasping of parallel bars or a cane. RAGT with the Morning Walk system began on December 28, 2022 in ground-walk mode with an initial K-level 1 goal.

The first session used cadence 25 steps/min and 8% body-weight support, with cadence gradually increased to 45 steps/min, support reduced to 0% and stair-ascending mode at 40 steps/min; mean GRF improved markedly. She ambulated 80 m with an elbow-support walker after two weeks, the goal rose to K-level 3, and silicone upper-limb prostheses were fabricated on April 12, 2023. She now walks independently on level ground and climbs stairs holding rails.

summary.text: A 51-year-old female developed necrosis of both hands and feet following inotropic treatment for hypoglycemic shock in 2021; it progressed despite initial conservative management. On June 19, 2023 she had autoamputation findings of the right ankle and wrist, left subtalar joint and left hand phalanges, and on June 26, 2023 underwent bilateral transtibial and right transradial amputations.

She was fitted with upper- and lower-limb prostheses on August 31, 2023 and began inpatient rehabilitation with a K-level 1 goal. RAGT in ground-walk mode began on September 1, 2023 at cadence 30 steps/min with 0% body-weight support. Worsening bilateral knee pain attributed to osteoarthritis reduced footplate loading and GRF, and hyaluronic acid injections were given on September 11 and October 10.

After the pain subsided cadence was increased to 50 steps/min, and after she began supervised level-ground walking RAGT progressed to stair-ascending mode. Before RAGT she could stand independently but needed minimal assistance to ambulate; after two weeks she used a Lofstrand crutch and after three weeks walked under supervision. Her K-level goal was revised from Level 1 to Level 3, and she now ambulates independently and manages stairs without support.

article_limitations: Case 1 ambulation level after five months is described as supervised in the results and as independent walking in the discussion; both facts are review_only source conflicts.

Case 1 text values for cadence 50 steps/min and GRFs of 96% (right) and 106% (left) after two months do not match the plotted data in Fig. 2A (maximum plotted cadence 45 steps/min, no right GRF of 96%); these facts are review_only source conflicts and the session number at two months is not stated.
Case 2 hyaluronic acid injection dates give day and month without a year; the route intra-articular comes from a later sentence naming these injections.
Case 2 "in 2021" ends a sentence covering the shock, inotropic treatment and necrosis and is applied as that sentence time to the shock and the necrosis.
Chart values in Fig. 2 are estimated from the plots in the separate visual target and are not recorded as text facts.
The article has no tables and no supplementary files.
